chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Mutt Carey talks Joe into Doc Heiner's theory class in Pasadena
summary: Mutt took lessons from symphony man Doc Heiner, whose backyard class in Pasadena Joe joined briefly, finding it over his head.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: As a matter of fact, they had a teacher here that taught the musicians that... He was a symphony man. His name was Doc Heiner. [SPELLS] He had his kind of school of music in Pasadena. I don't know why I went there in the first place, but Mutt was the cause of it.
Oh, you went there when you were out here in the Twenties, the late Twenties.

Yeah, when I was playing with Mutt. Mutt says, "I'm taking lessons from Doctor Heiner." He had like a little class in his back yard; he had a beautiful back yard in Pasadena, his garden like. And he had blackboards where he would demonstrate. He was too far ahead of me, really. I just threw my five dollars away.
It was like a group class, you mean.
Well, he would yes. And Papa Mutt and I would be there, and four or five other guys that played in the pit orchestras here, and some that played in the studios.
Anybody of any name that you can remember was in those classes?

Oh, I can remember they had a bandleader around there named Rube Wolf, who was a trombone player -- he used to take lessons. A couple of guys that was in Gus Arnheim's band. Gus had a little guy, a trumpet player named Roy Fox, who was his lead trumpet player, and another saxophone player named Fats something. But he mostly taught theory and harmony, and stuff that I shouldn't have been in, that's what I'm saying, but that damn Papa Mutt talked me into going there. And Papa Mutt had the nutty idea that Doc Heiner, he was such a great musician, and such other great musicians went out there to see him and took lessons, that he could probably improve his tone, so he could play better.
